name: org.polarka/polarka-agent
title: Polarka Agent: a NORTH wallet for agents
description: Pays x402 in NORTH. Free remote tools: network, guide, stamps. Keys can sit apart from the agent.

tools.name: north_network
tools.description: Live numbers of the TrueNorth (NORTH) chain: height, blocks of the last 24 hours, an estimate of the network's hashrate, the block reward, the coins issued so far and the next halving; and of the Polarka pool: its hashrate, miners, fee, payout scheme and blocks found. Read from the node and the pool at polarka.org; hashrates are estimates. Takes no arguments. Use it to answer how big or busy the network is, or before mining.

tools.name: north_guide
tools.description: Practical steps and links for one topic: "start" (what NORTH is, what it is good for, honest limits), "agent" (giving an agent its own wallet that pays within limits its owner sets), "mining" (pools and solo, with a fair comparison of fees), "wallet" (wallets for people and for coins kept offline, the faucet), "stamps" (how a stamp works and how anyone can check one). Returns text and links; nothing is changed.

tools.name: north_stamp
tools.description: Records that some data existed by a block: give the SHA-256 of a file or text (64 hexadecimal characters; compute it yourself and never send the data itself). Free of charge, within a daily bound for all callers together and a smaller one for the internet address a request comes from, which many users of one application may share. Stamps are written in batches about every ten minutes: the first answer says "waiting" and when the next batch is; call again with the same sha256 after it and one block (about 15 minutes in all) and the answer is the proof (state "stamped"). Asking again within seven days for a hash taken through this connector costs nothing. Keep the proof. Anyone can check it without trusting Polarka: polarka-agent stamp-verify with their own TrueNorth node, or the transaction and its block in an explorer of the chain. north_stamp_verify checks it here, with Polarka's node. The hash of a short or guessable text can be guessed back: add a random secret and keep it. TrueNorth is young and small: a stamp is evidence of order in time, not proof for a court.

sha256.description: the SHA-256 of the data, 64 hexadecimal characters

tools.name: north_stamp_verify
tools.description: Checks a proof of a stamp (the JSON that north_stamp returns in state "stamped", or a proof file of polarka-agent): that the path leads from the SHA-256 to the root, that the transaction carries the root, that the block holds the transaction, and with Polarka's node that this block is in the TrueNorth chain. Answers valid true with the block, its time and depth, or valid false with the reason. It is Polarka's server asking Polarka's node: to check without trusting Polarka, use polarka-agent stamp-verify with a node of your own.

proof.description: the proof, as north_stamp returned it
